clue.text: Boxer's big tummy?

parts.note: a big tummy is weight carried round the middle of the body, and the boxing class between welter and light-heavy is named the same way

explanation.surface: A joke about a prizefighter who has let himself go and grown a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Boxer's' as 'Boxer is': the fighter in this weight class is described as if he were a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a boxing division and a fighter in it, while literally suggesting bulk carried at the waist.

clue.text: Went for a drive in limo — tore downtown

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone took a ride in a limousine and tore through the city centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To have driven around in a car is the old-fashioned phrase for a jaunt by automobile.

clue.text: Ministry's juniors and seniors with incorporated company

indicators.note: the seniors take the company inside them

parts.note: deans are senior figures in a college or cathedral

explanation.surface: A government department's junior and senior staff join up with an incorporated firm.
explanation.definitionFit: In the church's ordained ministry these clergy rank below priests.

clue.text: Romeo breaks down in embrace of the French staff

indicators.note: the word for breaks down is held inside the other two pieces

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
to staff a desk is to man it
a car that breaks down dies

explanation.surface: Romeo goes to pieces in the arms of French staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a womaniser, a charmer who is popular with women.

clue.text: Some Brits oddly skipped this clue — two upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the kept letters read upwards
the odd-numbered letters of these words are passed over, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Some Britons skipped over this clue, leaving two people annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue' looks like self-reference, but its letters plus those of 'two' are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Wales form part of the population of Great Britain.

clue.text: Popular, healthier gadget some patients use

parts.note: something popular is in
hale means healthy, so haler is healthier

explanation.surface: A trendy health gadget that some patients have taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma sufferers use a puffer device to breathe medicine into the lungs.

clue.text: Try and eat earlier

parts.note: to have lunch is to eat it
ago means in the past, earlier

explanation.surface: Advice to sample something and to eat ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attempt something, to give it a shot.

clue.text: Separate up by Tesco's entrance — scrap heavy carrier

parts.note: a road that separates in two forks
to lift is to raise up

indicators.note: the entrance to the word is its first letter

parts.note: a ruck is a scrap, a brawl or rugby scramble

explanation.surface: A brawl erupts by the doors of a Tesco supermarket over a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco is a big British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small industrial vehicle with prongs raises and moves heavy pallets.

clue.text: Posh bore with CD that's entertaining crashed net once

parts.note: a bore is a borehole, a well

indicators.note: the letters CD hold the rearranged words inside them, as a host entertains guests
crashed means wrecked, so the letters of net once are jumbled

explanation.surface: An upper-class bore with a CD that once kept people amused when the internet crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with friends in high places moves in grand society.

clue.text: Blooming drag to go west from the centre

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left, so the word for drag is turned backwards

parts.note: to drag is to draw, as a cart is drawn

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to haul a load westward, away from the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward motion heads away from the middle, toward the exterior.

clue.text: Port in Spain — have to keep right following learner

indicators.note: the rest of the letters come after the learner's letter, so it goes at the front

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: the word have holds the letter for right inside it

explanation.surface: It looks like advice about a harbour in Spain where a novice must stay on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port in Spain' reads like the definition, but the port is French; 'in' is a link and Spain only supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: This Normandy city at the mouth of the Seine is one of France's chief seaports.

clue.text: Singing challenge in middle of 'Mikado' excited Korea

indicators.note: the two central letters of the word Mikado are taken
excited letters are stirred up, so Korea is rearranged

explanation.surface: Korea gets worked up over a vocal contest staged midway through Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar-room sing-along entertainment where amateurs perform to backing tracks is a test of nerve and voice.

clue.text: Lobby to acquire vintage bag

indicators.note: the hall takes in the other piece, holding it within

parts.note: a lobby or entrance area is a hall
vintage things are old

explanation.surface: A lobbying group sets out to buy an antique handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A large travelling bag that takes everything is a type of luggage carrier.

clue.text: River business lacking endeavour

indicators.note: lacking means the word for endeavour is missing from the longer word

parts.note: business as a sector of commerce is industry
to endeavour is to try

explanation.surface: A river trade that has lost its drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A great waterway flowing from Tibet through Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Steward, soldier and medic hosting party

indicators.note: the soldier and medic together hold the party between them

parts.note: a major is an army officer
MO is a medical officer
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A household servant, an army man and a doctor are throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief servant who runs a great house is its head butler or steward.

clue.text: Knave, loud sort, agitated very cool character

parts.note: the knave in cards is the jack
F is forte, loud in music

indicators.note: agitated means stirred, so the letters of sort are mixed

explanation.surface: A rogue, a noisy type, gets worked up into a really chilled figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The personification of frost and wintry cold is a literally chilly figure.

clue.text: Used in rolling Plasticine gel, ethylene's effective on a screen

indicators.note: rolling turns the found letters over so they read backwards
the letters used are found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lab note about Plasticine, gel and ethylene being rolled together to work on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes across well on television or film looks good to camera.

clue.text: Burlesque item lit up by old nurse with nothing on

parts.words: item lit up by old nurse
parts.note: Florence Nightingale, the Victorian nurse, was 'the Lady with the Lamp'
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A saucy stage show features an old nurse with a light and wearing nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirical send-up or parody ridicules its target by mockery.

clue.text: Cavalier's horse jumping everything, over time

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the combined letters are read backwards
the horse leaps over and around the word for everything, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
all means everything

explanation.surface: A Royalist's horse clears every fence, though over the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing, courtly gentleman, like a Royalist cavalier, is chivalrous and brave.

clue.text: Mother stuffing turkey, maybe — this one's tough

indicators.note: the mother goes inside the bird like stuffing

parts.note: a female turkey, like any female fowl, is a hen
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mum is stuffing the Christmas turkey, which turns out to be a tough old bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly muscled, macho man is the type described as tough.

clue.text: 'Phone home!' offering top part with small alien

indicators.note: in a down clue the top part of a word is its first letter

parts.note: and means with, together
S is small, as in clothing sizes
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: E.T.'s famous plea to 'phone home', given with a little alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone home!' is E.T.'s line in Spielberg's film, which makes 'alien' feel like part of the quote.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a telephone you lift and hold is a telephone receiver.

clue.text: University taken in by corrupt master for ages

indicators.note: the university letter is held inside the jumbled word
corrupt means spoilt or twisted, so the letters of master are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university is fooled for years by a crooked headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow older or ripen over time is the verb sense of the definition.

clue.text: Wound oozed after shove

indicators.note: the word for oozed comes after the word for shove

parts.note: to shove is to ram
blood oozed, or bled, from a cut

explanation.surface: An injury seeped blood after someone was pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, as a road winds.
explanation.definitionFit: A path that meandered or twisted about is said to have wandered aimlessly.

clue.text: Alarm seeing daughter study

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A parent is alarmed to see their daughter studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and apprehension are the noun senses shared by both words.

clue.text: Cooler loft with central extraction is radical

parts.note: a fan cools the air

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for loft is taken out

parts.note: a loft is an attic

explanation.surface: A ventilation spec: a cooling unit in the loft with central extraction is a radical idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist, zealous in their views, is a radical in the noun sense.

clue.text: Hymn and carol he orchestrated

indicators.note: orchestrated means arranged, so these letters are scored afresh

explanation.surface: A hymn and a carol that one man arranged for orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately chorus sung in church, as in Bach's settings of Lutheran tunes, is a sacred song.

clue.text: Remember watch, say

definitions.meaning: to remember an anniversary is to keep or mark it, as with a minute's silence
to watch is to look at carefully
to say something is to remark on it

explanation.surface: Remember to keep an eye on things, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is a third definition: to remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers keeping a custom, looking closely, and passing a comment.

clue.text: Country with two capitals where our people may be represented

definitions.text: Country with two capitals where our people may be represented

parts.words: Country with two capitals where our people may be represented
parts.note: the nation's short form is two capital letters, and it is a federation whose governed parts, as members of a union, send representatives to Congress

explanation.surface: A description of a nation with two seats of government where people like us have a voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two capitals' suggests two capital cities, but means the two capital letters of the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a federal republic of fifty member regions, abbreviated to US.
